sections.title: Political Psychology & Democratic Backsliding in the US
sections.description: This course surveys major theoretical approaches and empirical research in the study of democratic backsliding and erosion across the mass public. We will focus primarily on American politics, although many of the theoretical perspectives are applicable outside the United States. Among the topics we will address are the underpinning of threat that motivate erosion, support for political violence, reactions, and reinterpretations of events of erosion, and authoritarian elites and their use of rhetoric for the sake of consolidating power. This course has three learning objectives: You will analyze contemporary debates in the study of democratic backsliding. You will think both appreciatively and critically about social scientific research. You will develop a research question and make progress on the question throughout the course.
